decisions.decision: Corpus scope: index the 757 security relevant unique documents, and keep the full set of 4,007 unique documents as a second search area.
decisions.why: The security subset covers the skill domain. The remainder answers an adjacent question.

decisions.decision: Storage split: the repository holds the skill only, within a budget of 400 KB across 10 files or less. The 744 MB of converted Markdown stays outside the repository at the corpus root.
decisions.why: The largest existing skill is 140 KB. The repository is OneDrive synced. The converted text is also copyrighted.

decisions.decision: Retrieval: a router SKILL.md, a curated reference set, one index file, and a written search procedure. No helper script is committed.
decisions.why: This mirrors managing-mist-api. An agent reads a small router first, then opens only the reference that the task needs.

decisions.decision: Conversion quality: ten acceptance rules, a floor of 200 characters per page, and a manual audit of 30 documents.
decisions.why: The converter has a known weakness on cover pages.

decisions.decision: Deduplication: the newest readable train wins, with fallback to the next newest readable train. The index records the train used, the newest train available, and a supersedes field.
decisions.why: A document repeats across trains 21.1 to 26.2, and the newest copy is not always readable.

decisions.decision: The index holds 775 rows, not 757. Membership is: the catalog security flag (710), the FR-007 term match on the file name (38), and a named checklist-need list (27), minus 8 documents below the 200-characters-per-page floor.
decisions.why: No rule reproduces 757. The term rule alone misses routing-policy.pdf, network-mgmt.pdf, time-mgmt.pdf, icmp.pdf, junos-install-upgrade.pdf, and the routing protocol guides, which 6 of the 8 checklist sections need.

decisions.decision: The skill never cites a path below documentation/references/. It cites a public URL first and the corpus root path second, which follows the 15 committed noc-runbooks.
decisions.why: git check-ignore shows .gitignore line 28 ignores that directory because it holds verbatim vendor text. git ls-files returns 0 files, and Test-Path returns False in a fresh worktree.

decisions.decision: Upgrade the committed scripts/pdf_to_markdown.py so the documented rebuild command reproduces the staged corpus. The skill folder still ships documentation only.
decisions.why: .gitignore lines 20 to 28 already promise that command. The committed script writes a flat page dump with no front matter and no heading detection, so the promise is false today.

decisions.decision: Use pdfplumber for the upgraded converter. Do not add PyMuPDF. Check V15 tests the structural contract of 30 sample files, not a byte match against the staged corpus.
decisions.why: PyMuPDF is dual licensed under AGPL-3.0, and container-build.yml pushes to ghcr.io, which is distribution. pdfplumber is MIT, pyproject.toml already declares it, and the char size key gives the font size that the heading rule needs at about 5 times slower, which is 0.3 hours for a full rebuild.

specify.summary: The spec for the hardening-junos project skill is written and validated. It settles the corpus scope, the storage split, the retrieval design, the conversion quality criteria, and the deduplication rule.
specify.key_finding: The corpus is too large for the repository, so the skill holds curated guidance plus one index, and the bulk text stays on disk outside the repository.

plan.summary: The implementation plan and its design artifacts are written and then revised against 3 repository facts. The skill ships 6 files at about 262 KB. The corpus of 744 MB stays outside the repository, and the plan upgrades the committed converter.
plan.key_finding: documentation/references/ is ignored on purpose, so the repository already runs the vendor-text policy that the spec proposes. The committed scripts/pdf_to_markdown.py must be upgraded with pdfplumber, not PyMuPDF, because the container image is a distribution and the AGPL applies.
